veranderings.voor: en dan swel dit dikker op
veranderings.na: en dan swel dit op en word dikker
veranderings.rede: 'swel dikker op' is an awkward combination, because 'opswel' already means growing bigger; splitting it keeps both ideas and reads naturally.
Two attributive adjectives before a noun read more naturally separated by a comma than joined by 'en', especially straight after the list 'lank, dun en swak'.

veranderings.voor: Kyk na 'n plant in 'n pot met blare aan sy stam
veranderings.na: Kyk na 'n potplant met blare aan sy stam
veranderings.rede: As written, 'met blare aan sy stam' can attach to 'pot'; 'potplant', the word the lesson uses later, removes the ambiguity.

veranderings.voor: Watter saad dink jy ontkiem eerste?
veranderings.na: Watter saad, dink jy, ontkiem eerste?
veranderings.rede: 'dink jy' is an inserted clause here and is set off by commas, which also keeps the reader from reading 'saad dink' together.

vlae.teks: Later druk 'n klein stingel boontoe by die saad uit.
vlae.rede: The lesson calls this part 'stam' everywhere else (including the measuring list, 'die hoogte van die stam'); 'stingel' here may read as a different part to a Grade 4 learner. Not changed because it is a subject term and the choice is the writer's.
